newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Worries, profit-taking hit Bel-20, outlook mixed.
newsitem.headline: Worries, profit-taking hit Bel-20, outlook mixed.

text.p: Worries that rises in bonds would not last and pre-Christmas profit-taking pushed the Bel-20 index softly into the red on Tuesday despite gains by the Dow Jones dealers said.
Dealers were mixed over the outlook for the Belgian index.

Steel maker Cockerill Sambre was the biggest loser, falling 4.1 percent to 116 francs. Heavy selling came in afternoon trade ahead of Cockerill's Bel-20 departure on December 20. "There's been some Bel-20 reshuffeling today with investors dumping Cockerill shares and buying Barco as it will replace Cockerill in the Bel-20," said a trader.
Dealers were mixed over whether the bourse would see large rises before the New Year, but interest rate fears or large Dow Jones movements could push investors once again into the market.
"The bourse won't improve before Christmas because people will focus on their balance sheets, settling accounts, taking profits or going on holiday," said one trader.

Another trader said "traditionally December and January are good months with a lot of money coming onto the market, but after the rises we've seen this year I'm not sure we we'll see the traditional Christmas rises".
Oil and chemicals firm Petrofina fell 2.16 percent to 10,175 francs, continuing the underperformance of recent weeks, but with good potential for 1997.
"Petrofina will go up again probably at the end of the month or early in 1997," said a trader.
Another said the stock did not look good because "the market is faced with the fact that the refinery margins are weak and this will not help Petrofina".
He added the fall in Petrofina could be due to self-made Belgian magnate Baron Albert Frere selling parts of his Petrofina stake to buy into other sectors in Belgium.
"There's some speculation in the market that Frere is getting rid of some stocks to buy Havas shares," he said.

Elsewhere dealers welcomed Tessenderlo's buy of Chelsea Bridge Building Products, a U.S. plastic profiles for windows and doors producer. One dealer said, "the takeover was very important for the company's future".
